skills.name: Council of High Intelligence
skills.summary: 18 thinker personas (Feynman, Taleb, Munger, Torvalds, Socrates and more) deliberate a hard decision. They analyse blind first, cross-examine each other anonymously, then vote. A chairman writes the verdict, including what would prove it wrong and one concrete next step.

spend.idle: ~650 tokens per session (the 18 agent descriptions). The skill itself loads only when you call it.
spend.perUse: --quick or --duo: ~50–90k tokens. Default (3 personas): ~120–250k. --full (all 18): ~1–1.5M, about 100× a normal answer.

bestFor: Decisions that are expensive to reverse: pricing, architecture, launch plans
"Should multi-person splitting be free or Pro?"-type product calls
Stress-testing a plan you're already leaning towards
avoid: Coding tasks, factual lookups, anything a test can answer
--full: going from 3 to 18 personas costs a lot and adds little
howTo: On the laptop add --no-auto-route to keep seats off your local Ollama model
skills.notes: Local patches: runs only when you type /council; Codex seats are read-only; personas can't run shell commands. See skills/council/LOCAL_PATCHES.md.

skills.name: LLM Council (light)
skills.summary: Your original council, renamed so it doesn't clash with /council. Opus, Sonnet and Haiku each answer the question on their own, rank each other's answers anonymously, and the main session writes a synthesis.
bestFor: A quick second opinion from several models without personas or a formal verdict
avoid: Overlaps with /council --quick, so consider retiring one
skills.notes: Was called /council on the branch claude/github-skip-scope-investigation-7EiT4 and mirrored to the laptop. The setup script moves the old laptop copy to _conflicts.

skills.name: Prompt Master
skills.summary: Turns a rough idea into one paste-ready prompt tuned for a specific AI tool, such as Claude Code, Cursor, ChatGPT, Midjourney or Sora. It asks at most 3 clarifying questions, and for agent tools it adds file-scope limits, stop conditions and checkpoints.

spend.perUse: ~7k tokens, plus up to ~6k when it loads its templates. About the cost of one normal answer.

bestFor: Mega-prompts for Claude Code or Cursor
Adapting a prompt for another AI tool
Fixing a prompt that keeps giving weak results
avoid: Nothing to avoid: it stays dormant unless you ask for a prompt
howTo: "Write me a Claude Code prompt to …" (starts automatically)

skills.name: REA: Reverse Engineer Anything
skills.summary: Inspects shipped apps without their source code: native binaries, Electron/JavaScript apps, .NET, Android, firmware and websites. It explains how a feature works, with the evidence and limits behind each conclusion. Analysis runs locally.

spend.idle: ~75 tokens per session (skill description), plus the MCP tool list. That list is large (~180 tools), but Claude Code holds big tool sets back until needed.
spend.perUse: ~6k tokens for the skill and up to ~13k for references when it loads them. Decompiled output can add 20–200k depending on the target.

bestFor: "How does app X implement feature Y?" on software you're allowed to analyse
Checking what's inside your own builds (SplitEven APK/AAB, Electron bundles)
Security review of your own shipped artifacts
avoid: Normal source repos (just read the code)
DRM or licence bypass, cheats, anything a target's terms forbid (see the project's DISCLAIMER)
howTo: Needs Node.js; setup.ps1 registers the 'rea' MCP server pinned to 6.5.0
For native binaries install Ghidra (free); Hopper is macOS-only
Check it's connected: claude mcp list
skills.notes: Responsible-use policy in the upstream DISCLAIMER.md applies.

skills.name: OpenMontage
skills.invoke: Open Claude Code inside its folder
skills.summary: A video production studio your coding agent runs: research, script, stock or AI-generated footage, narration, a Remotion edit and the final render. It ships 49 skills of its own that only load while you work inside its folder.

spend.idle: Nothing outside its folder. About 2k tokens of skill descriptions while you work in it.
spend.perUse: A full video run is token-heavy (estimate: several hundred k), plus provider charges if you use paid video or voice APIs. The free route uses stock footage and local tools.

bestFor: Promo and explainer videos, e.g. a 9:16 or Portuguese cut of the SplitEven launch video
avoid: Installing its 49 skills globally: they depend on its own tools
Face-swap or avatar features without the depicted person's consent
howTo: Follow its README Quick Start (Python venv + requirements, Node for remotion-composer, ffmpeg)
Copy .env.example to .env and add only the keys you'll use
Run claude there and describe the video
skills.notes: Cloned by setup.ps1 at the reviewed commit; not stored in this repo (AGPL, 92 MB).
